usageNotes: Permanently deletes a named LXC snapshot and its associated disk data; the operation is asynchronous and returns a UPID task ID that should be polled to confirm completion. The caller must hold the VM.Snapshot privilege on /vms/{vmid}, and the target node must be online. Use the `force` parameter only as a last resort when disk snapshot removal fails and you want to at least clean the config entry — disk data may then be orphaned.

examples.summary: Delete a pre-upgrade snapshot named 'before_upgrade' from LXC 110 on node pve1

destructiveReason: Permanently removes the snapshot and its stored disk state; this data cannot be recovered after deletion.
tips: Poll the returned UPID via the tasks API to confirm the snapshot was fully removed before taking further snapshot actions on the same CT.
Deleting a snapshot with a child snapshot (rollback chain) is not supported; remove descendants first.
If the LXC uses an overlayfs/dir-based rootfs, snapshot deletion is typically instant; for ZFS or LVM-thin it may take longer depending on data size.
The `force` flag bypasses disk-layer removal errors but can leave orphaned volumes on the storage — audit storage afterward if used.
